subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan is situated in:
explanation: Pakistan lies in the north-west of the South Asian subcontinent, alongside India, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan has borders with ______ and ______.
explanation: Pakistan’s land neighbours are India, China, Afghanistan and Iran; it has no land border with the Gulf states or the Central Asian republics.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan lies roughly between the latitudes of:
explanation: Pakistan extends from about 24° N on the Sindh coast to about 37° N in the far north of Gilgit-Baltistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan Standard Time is:
explanation: Pakistan observes a single time zone five hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time; UTC +5:30 is India’s and UTC +4:30 is Afghanistan’s.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Excluding Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, the area of Pakistan is about:
explanation: The standard figure for the four provinces and Islamabad is 796,096 square kilometres; 652,230 sq km is roughly the area of Afghanistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from:
explanation: The narrow Wakhan strip of Afghanistan’s Badakhshan province lies between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan in the south and Tajikistan in the north.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan shares its shortest international border with:
explanation: The Pakistan–China border in Gilgit-Baltistan is only a few hundred kilometres long, shorter than the borders with Iran, Afghanistan and India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and:
explanation: The Durand Line, drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan, forms Pakistan’s western border with Afghanistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which province of Pakistan shares a border with Iran?
explanation: Balochistan is the only province adjoining Iran; the border runs from the Chagai area down to Gwadar Bay.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which two provinces of Pakistan border Afghanistan?
explanation: The Durand Line runs along Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (including the former tribal districts) and northern Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which part of Pakistan shares a border with China?
explanation: Pakistan’s border with China’s Xinjiang region lies entirely in Gilgit-Baltistan, crossed by the Karakoram Highway at Khunjerab.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which provinces of Pakistan share the international border with India?
explanation: The Pakistan–India international boundary runs along Punjab and Sindh; further north the Line of Control divides Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Taftan, in Chagai district, is a border crossing between Pakistan and:
explanation: Taftan lies on the Quetta–Zahedan route and is the main road and rail crossing into Iran.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Wagah border crossing lies on the road between Lahore and:
explanation: Wagah–Attari is the main land crossing between Pakistan and India, on the Grand Trunk Road between Lahore and Amritsar.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The coastal town of Jiwani lies close to Pakistan’s border with:
explanation: Jiwani is on Gwadar Bay at the western end of the Makran coast, next to the Iranian border.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The largest province of Pakistan by area is:
explanation: Balochistan covers about 44 percent of Pakistan’s area, though it is the least populated province.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The smallest province of Pakistan by area is:
explanation: Even after the merger of the former tribal areas, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is smaller in area than Sindh, Punjab and Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Before 2009, Gilgit-Baltistan was officially known as the:
explanation: The region was renamed Gilgit-Baltistan under the Gilgit-Baltistan (Empowerment and Self-Governance) Order of 2009.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Muzaffarabad is the capital of:
explanation: Muzaffarabad, at the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers, is the seat of the AJK government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The word ‘Punjab’ means:
explanation: Punjab comes from Persian panj (five) and ab (water), referring to the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Faisalabad was formerly known as:
explanation: Lyallpur was renamed Faisalabad in 1977 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia; Montgomery is now Sahiwal and Campbellpur is Attock.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sahiwal was formerly called:
explanation: The town was named Montgomery after Sir Robert Montgomery, a Lieutenant-Governor of the Punjab, and was later renamed Sahiwal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which city is known as the ‘Fruit Garden of Pakistan’?
explanation: Quetta’s valley is famous for apples, grapes, apricots and other temperate fruits grown in its orchards.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The highest peak in Pakistan is:
explanation: K2 (8,611 m) is Pakistan’s highest mountain and the second highest in the world after Everest.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: K2 is located in the:
explanation: K2 stands on the Pakistan–China border in the Baltoro section of the Karakoram.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The height of K2 is:
explanation: K2 is 8,611 metres high; 8,848 m is Everest, 8,126 m Nanga Parbat and 8,051 m Broad Peak.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: K2 was first climbed in 1954 by an expedition from:
explanation: The Italian expedition led by Ardito Desio put Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni on the summit on 31 July 1954.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Pakistani peak is popularly called the ‘Killer Mountain’?
explanation: Nanga Parbat earned the name after many climbers died on it before its first ascent in 1953; K2 is called the ‘Savage Mountain’.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Nanga Parbat lies in which mountain range?
explanation: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the western anchor of the Great Himalaya, south of the Indus bend near Chilas.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, is in:
explanation: Tirich Mir (about 7,700 m) rises in Upper Chitral and dominates the Hindu Kush on the Pakistani side.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: How many of the world’s fourteen peaks above 8,000 metres are in Pakistan?
explanation: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II are the five eight-thousanders in Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Rakaposhi peak rises above the:
explanation: Rakaposhi (about 7,788 m) in the Karakoram stands over the Nagar Valley and is a landmark on the Karakoram Highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Himalaya, Karakoram and Hindu Kush ranges meet near:
explanation: A point on the Karakoram Highway near Juglot in Gilgit district is marked as the junction of the three great ranges.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pamir Knot, north of Pakistan, is often called the:
explanation: The high Pamir plateau, where several great ranges converge, is traditionally called the Roof of the World.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Margalla Hills around Islamabad are foothills of the:
explanation: The Margallas form the southernmost outliers of the lesser Himalaya overlooking the Potohar Plateau.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kirthar Range forms a natural boundary between:
explanation: The Kirthar Range runs north–south along the western edge of the Indus plain, separating Sindh from Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Salt Range forms the southern edge of the:
explanation: The Salt Range rises between the Jhelum and the Indus and separates the Potohar Plateau from the Punjab plains to the south.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which plateau lies between the Jhelum and Indus rivers in northern Punjab?
explanation: The Potohar Plateau around Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum lies between the two rivers, north of the Salt Range.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Malika Parbat, the highest peak of the Kaghan Valley, overlooks:
explanation: Malika Parbat (‘Queen of the Mountains’) towers over Lake Saiful Muluk near Naran.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Fairy Meadows is famous for its close views of:
explanation: Fairy Meadows lies near Raikot in Diamer district at the base of Nanga Parbat’s Raikot face.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Karoonjhar Hills are located in:
explanation: The granite Karoonjhar Hills rise from the Thar Desert at Nagarparkar in the south-east corner of Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The world’s highest battlefield, the Siachen Glacier, is located in which mountain range?
explanation: Siachen lies in the eastern Karakoram, north of the Saltoro Ridge, where Pakistani and Indian troops have faced each other since 1984.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Batura Glacier is located in:
explanation: The Batura Glacier flows eastward from the Batura Muztagh to the Hunza River near Passu, next to the Karakoram Highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Baltoro Glacier, which leads trekkers towards K2, lies in the:
explanation: The Baltoro Glacier in Baltistan runs to Concordia, surrounded by K2, Broad Peak and the Gasherbrums.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Snow Lake (Lukpe Lawo) lies at the head of the Biafo Glacier, which connects over the Hispar La with the:
explanation: The Biafo and Hispar glaciers meet at the Hispar La near Snow Lake, forming one long glacial route across the central Karakoram.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Concordia, the camp below K2, is the confluence of the Baltoro and the:
explanation: At Concordia the Godwin-Austen Glacier from K2 joins the upper Baltoro Glacier.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with:
explanation: The Karakoram Highway crosses into China’s Xinjiang region over the Khunjerab Pass in Gilgit-Baltistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khyber Pass links Pakistan with:
explanation: The Khyber Pass runs from near Peshawar to Torkham on the Afghan border, on the historic route to Kabul.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with:
explanation: The Bolan Pass carries the road and railway from the Kachhi plain near Sibi up to the Quetta valley.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lowari Pass, now bypassed by a tunnel, connects Dir with:
explanation: The Lowari Pass and the Lowari Tunnel link Upper Dir with Chitral, which was cut off by snow in winter before the tunnel.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khojak Pass and tunnel lie on the route between Quetta and:
explanation: The Khojak Tunnel through the Toba Kakar hills carries the railway from Quetta towards Chaman on the Afghan border.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Babusar Pass connects the Kaghan Valley with:
explanation: The road over the Babusar Pass at the head of the Kaghan Valley descends to Chilas on the Karakoram Highway.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Shandur Pass, famous for its polo festival, links Chitral with:
explanation: Shandur lies between Chitral and the Ghizer district of Gilgit-Baltistan; teams from the two regions meet there each summer.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Mintaka Pass, an old Silk Road crossing from Hunza, leads into:
explanation: The Mintaka Pass on the Pakistan–China border was the main caravan route from Hunza to Xinjiang before the Khunjerab route was built.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The longest river of Pakistan is the:
explanation: The Indus flows the whole length of Pakistan from Gilgit-Baltistan to the Arabian Sea.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indus River rises in:
explanation: The Indus rises in western Tibet near Lake Mansarovar and flows through Ladakh before entering Gilgit-Baltistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which river is called ‘Abaseen’, the father of rivers?
explanation: Abaseen is the Pashto name for the Indus, meaning ‘father of rivers’.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which river joins the Indus near Attock?
explanation: The Kabul River, after flowing through the Peshawar valley, meets the Indus near Attock.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The combined waters of the Punjab rivers flow from Panjnad into the Indus near:
explanation: The Panjnad River, formed by the Chenab and Sutlej systems, joins the Indus near Mithankot in Rajanpur district.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Lahore is situated on the bank of the river:
explanation: Lahore grew on the left bank of the Ravi, one of the eastern rivers allotted to India under the Indus Waters Treaty.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Jhelum River rises at:
explanation: The Jhelum rises from the Verinag spring in the Kashmir Valley and passes through Wular Lake before entering Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Gilgit River is a tributary of the:
explanation: The Gilgit River, joined by the Hunza River, falls into the Indus near Bunji.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Swat River flows into the:
explanation: The Swat River leaves the Swat Valley and joins the Kabul River in the Charsadda area of the Peshawar valley.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which river flows through the Kaghan Valley?
explanation: The Kunhar River drains the Kaghan Valley past Naran and Balakot and joins the Jhelum near Muzaffarabad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Neelum River joins the Jhelum at:
explanation: The Neelum meets the Jhelum at Domel in Muzaffarabad, the capital of Azad Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In Afghanistan, the Chitral River is known as the:
explanation: The Chitral River flows south-west into Afghanistan as the Kunar, which later joins the Kabul River.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Indus River falls into the:
explanation: The Indus reaches the Arabian Sea through its delta south of Thatta in Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Rechna Doab lies between the rivers:
explanation: Rechna (Ra from Ravi and china from Chenab) is the doab containing Gujranwala, Sheikhupura and Faisalabad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Thal Desert lies in which doab?
explanation: Thal lies between the Indus and the Jhelum–Chenab, the Sindh Sagar Doab, covering Bhakkar, Layyah and Khushab.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Thar Desert in Pakistan lies mainly in:
explanation: In Pakistan the Thar Desert covers the Tharparkar region of south-eastern Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Cholistan Desert is located in:
explanation: Cholistan lies in the Bahawalpur division of southern Punjab, along the border with India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kharan Desert is located in:
explanation: Kharan is a sandy desert basin in north-western Balochistan, south of the Chagai hills.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Ziarat is known for its:
explanation: The Ziarat valley has one of the largest and oldest juniper forests in the world and is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s mangrove forests are found mainly in the:
explanation: Mangroves grow in the tidal creeks of the Indus delta and at a few points along the Balochistan coast.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Changa Manga, a large irrigated plantation forest, is in the district of:
explanation: Changa Manga was planted in the nineteenth century south-west of Lahore and lies in Kasur district.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Makran coast lies in the province of:
explanation: The Makran coast stretches from Hub to Jiwani and makes up roughly three-quarters of Pakistan’s coastline; Sindh has the shorter share around Karachi and the Indus delta.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which island is known as ‘Jazira Haft Talar’, the island of seven hills?
explanation: Astola lies in the Arabian Sea off Pasni on the Makran coast; its local name refers to its seven hills.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first Marine Protected Area was declared in 2017 at:
explanation: Astola Island was notified as Pakistan’s first Marine Protected Area in 2017 to protect coral, turtles and seabirds.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s territorial waters extend to:
explanation: Under Pakistan’s Maritime Zones Act and UNCLOS, the territorial sea is 12 nautical miles; 200 nautical miles marks the Exclusive Economic Zone.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In 2015 the UN accepted Pakistan’s claim extending its continental shelf to:
explanation: The UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf endorsed Pakistan’s submission in 2015, extending the shelf from 200 to 350 nautical miles.
